newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Mirage '97 estimate cut.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Mirage '97 estimate cut.

text.p: -- Bear, Stearns & Co analyst Jason Ader said he cut his 1997 estimate for Mirage Resorts Inc to $1.13/shr from $1.17 after Mirage's first quarter earnings dipped below analysts' consensus. On Tuesday, Mirage reported earnings of $0.29 a share, after a $0.01/shr charge, versus consensus of $0.31 and 1996's Q1 of $0.33 a share.

-- Ader noted one year ago, Mirage posted strong baccarat winnings, making 1997's Q1 comparison difficult. Moreover, in Las Vegas, Mirage was hurt by construction at the Golden Nugget hotel and by the closing of the Sands hotel, which decreased traffic at Mirage's nearby Treasure Island casino.
-- He also said growth of revenue per average room (REVPAR) was slightly below his expectation due to the increased supply of new hotel rooms in the Las Vegas market.
-- For the remainder of 1997, he had assumed REVPAR growth of 2.5 percent, but he reduced that figure to one percent, which in turn led to the reduction in his 1997 estimate.
-- Ader, however, maintained a buy rating on the stock based on increased cash flow from the new Bellagio hotel in Las Vegas in 1998. He also maintained his 1998 estimate at $1.40 a share.
-- Mirage shares were off 1-1/4 at 20-3/8 by midday.
